tool_args.content:
Single-panel causal directed acyclic graph (DAG) for a top-venue academic paper (EMNLP 2026).
Single column width, figsize (4.2, 3.8) inches, 300 DPI.

This is a causal diagram showing the assumed data-generating process for measuring style sensitivity in LLM judges.

LAYOUT: 5 nodes + 2 mechanism boxes arranged compactly:
- S (style) at center-left, Y (score) at center-right, on the same horizontal baseline
- Q (quality) above and between S and Y, slightly closer to Y
- P (position) below Y
- "Rewrite" box at top-left (above and left of S)
- "NLI gate" small box below the Rewrite box, between Rewrite and S

The layout should be COMPACT — no excessive whitespace. Nodes should be close enough that arrows are short and elegant.

NODES (circles):
All nodes are circles with diameter ~0.9cm equivalent (NOT too large), with very light colored fills and thin colored borders.

- S node: light academic blue fill (#4A6FA5 at 12% opacity), blue border (#4A6FA5) 0.8pt,
  bold label "S" in 13pt dark charcoal (#2C3E50), italic sub-label "style" in 8pt muted blue below
- Y node: same blue style as S, label "Y", sub-label "score"
- Q node: light sage green fill (#5B8C5A at 12% opacity), green border (#5B8C5A) 0.8pt,
  label "Q", sub-label "quality"
- P node: light neutral gray fill (#95A5A6 at 12% opacity), gray border (#95A5A6) 0.8pt,
  label "P", sub-label "position"

MECHANISM BOXES:
- "Rewrite" box: rounded rectangle (corner radius 6px), warm amber fill (#D4956A at 10% opacity),
  amber border (#D4956A) 0.8pt, italic label "Rewrite" in 10pt
- "NLI gate" box: smaller rounded rectangle, dashed purple border (#7E57C2 at 50% opacity) 0.7pt,
  very light purple fill (#7E57C2 at 6% opacity), label "NLI gate" in 8pt

ARROWS — PRIMARY CAUSAL PATH (emphasized):
- S → Y: thick (1.1pt) academic blue (#4A6FA5) arrow with small refined arrowhead,
  label "style sensitivity" in 8pt muted text centered below the arrow.
  This is the MAIN effect being measured — visually the most prominent arrow.

ARROWS — SECONDARY (thin gray):
- Q → Y: thin (0.7pt) dark gray (#555555 at 50% opacity) arrow, no label
- Rewrite → S: thin (0.7pt) dark gray arrow, no label

BLOCKED PATHS (THIN dash-dot style, muted red):
IMPORTANT: These blocked-path lines should be THIN (0.6pt) and ELEGANT, not thick or chunky.
Three paths that are blocked by experimental controls, drawn as thin dash-dot lines in muted red (#C0392B at 40% opacity) with small × symbols:
- Rewrite → Q: thin dash-dot red arrow with small red "×" at midpoint. This path is blocked by NLI gate.
- Rewrite → Y: thin dash-dot red arrow curving slightly, with small "× artifact" label in 7pt muted red.
  This path is blocked by double-rewrite control.
- P → Y: thin dash-dot red arrow with small "× swap" label in 7pt muted red.
  This path is blocked by position swapping.

RESIDUAL PATH:
- S → Q: thin dashed gray (#95A5A6 at 60% opacity) arrow curving upward from S to Q,
  with italic "residual" label in 7pt gray. This should be subtle and unobtrusive.

CONTROL ARROW:
- NLI gate → Rewrite: thin purple (#7E57C2 at 50% opacity) arrow, no label

CRITICAL STYLE REQUIREMENTS:
- Publication quality for EMNLP 2026 / NeurIPS level
- Elegant, premium, sophisticated — NOT cheap or homework-like
- ALL lines should be THIN and refined — no thick chunky lines except S→Y primary arrow
- Very subtle drop shadows on all nodes and boxes: 1.5px offset, 5% opacity maximum
- Rounded corners 6px on rectangular boxes
- Arrow heads: SMALL, refined triangular — NOT large or chunky. Maximum arrowhead size 4pt.
- The × markers should be small and elegant, not large or overwhelming
- Muted, harmonious color palette — no saturated or neon colors
- Pure white background (#FFFFFF)
- NO matplotlib defaults: no axes, no spines, no ticks, no gridlines, no gray background
- COMPACT layout: minimize whitespace, keep the diagram tight
- The overall feel: a figure from a Nature Methods or NeurIPS best paper
- When printed at column width (~3.25 inches), all text must be ≥ 7pt readable

14-\subsection{Content Preservation Verification}
15-\label{sec:nli_gate}
16-
17:Style-controlled rewriting risks altering semantic content, which would confound the style effect with a content quality effect (the $R \to Q$ path in Figure~\ref{fig:dag}).
18-To block this path, we apply a natural language inference (NLI) gate using DeBERTa-v3-large fine-tuned on MNLI \citep{williams2018broad} with an entailment threshold of 0.90, selected as the threshold above which NLI performance plateaus (Appendix~\ref{app:nli_sweep}).
19-For axes that preserve information density (formality, register), we apply standard bidirectional entailment: both NLI(original $\to$ rewrite) and NLI(rewrite $\to$ original) must exceed this value.
20-For axes that inherently change information density (e.g., verbosity), bidirectional verification is inappropriate---expansion necessarily introduces new content that the original cannot entail.
21-We instead apply direction-aware verification: for expansions, only backward entailment (rewrite entails original); for compressions, only forward entailment (original entails rewrite).
22-This recovered verbosity from 65\% to 86\% pass rate without inflating the effect estimate; for formality, strict bidirectional gating is necessary (Appendix~\ref{app:gate_validation}).
